comment: Seccomp BPF filter for QEMU/KVM and Firecracker backend VMs. Spec 038 FR-015.6. Allowlist approach: only the syscalls QEMU actually needs are permitted; everything else is rejected with EPERM. Derived from upstream QEMU's recommended seccomp config + devshot-specific hardening. devshot-sandbox-init compiles it to classic BPF (cmd/sandbox-init/seccomp.go) and installs it right before it execs QEMU; QEMU then stacks its own -sandbox filter on top (spawn/elevateprivileges/obsolete/resourcecontrol denied), which is why seccomp(2) itself is allowed: a stacked filter can only narrow this one.

syscalls.comment: File I/O (QEMU opens qcow2, sockets, pid files)

Threads only: clone without any namespace flag (CLONE_NEWNS|NEWCGROUP|NEWUTS|NEWIPC|NEWUSER|NEWPID|NEWNET = 0x7e020000). A compromised QEMU must not open a fresh user namespace (the gateway to most unprivileged kernel LPEs) or any other namespace. Both shipped architectures pass the flags in args[0].
clone3 passes its flags in a struct seccomp cannot read, so it answers ENOSYS and glibc falls back to the filtered clone above (the same move as Docker's default profile).
Sockets of AF_UNIX (QMP/QGA/console), AF_INET/AF_INET6 and AF_NETLINK only; AF_ALG, AF_VSOCK, AF_PACKET, AF_XDP, AF_KEY, AF_TIPC, AF_RDS and the rest stay closed. Rules for one syscall are ORed.
personality: only the plain Linux personas and the query (Docker's default set). READ_IMPLIES_EXEC and ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE stay closed.
QEMU's own -sandbox filter (and libseccomp's probe for it). Stacked seccomp filters can only narrow what this profile allows.

9p mapped-xattr ownership (spec 228). The virtio-9p xenstore share runs security_model=mapped-xattr: the guest-visible uid/gid/mode live in user.virtfs.* xattrs that dom0 seeds before QEMU starts. QEMU's local backend reads them with lgetxattr/fgetxattr on every stat and stamps them with lsetxattr on every create; without these the guest sees the host sandbox uid, root cannot enter its own 0700 share, and the DomU agent's ready=1 write dies with EPERM — the pool never becomes claimable. utimensat is the same backend's setattr(times) path.

comment_blocked: The following syscalls are EXPLICITLY BLOCKED (they hit defaultAction=ERRNO): ptrace, mount, umount2, pivot_root, reboot, kexec_load, init_module, finit_module, delete_module, setns, unshare, add_key, request_key, keyctl, create_module, nfsservctl, io_uring_enter, io_uring_setup, io_uring_register, process_vm_readv, process_vm_writev, kcmp, bpf, userfaultfd, perf_event_open, mknod, mknodat, swapon, swapoff, acct; clone/clone3 with any namespace flag, sockets outside AF_UNIX/AF_INET/AF_INET6/AF_NETLINK, personality outside PER_LINUX/PER_LINUX32.
